EXACT STOCHASTIC COMPILATION FROM IMPERFECT EXPERIMENTS
Working construction, 2026-10-31

Scientific claim and scope
==========================
The main object is an executable probability program, not an estimate of its
unknown numerical constants. Independent experimental bits supply those
constants during execution. A rational probability calculation with controlled
RELATIVE derivatives can be compiled into an exactly distributed output bit.
The construction has polynomial expected experimental, fair-bit, and ordinary
bit-computation cost. In particular its cost does not contain the reciprocal
of the output probability or of an intermediate positive partition function.

Existence of Bernoulli factories, smooth Bernstein envelopes, reverse-time
Bernstein algorithms, and Bernoulli races are established machinery. The
candidate new component here is a COMPUTATION-CHARGED multivariate lifting:
replace an exponentially large hypergeometric coefficient sum by a bounded,
nonnegative randomized correction, using a fixed-order Taylor control and a
tractable sum of product envelopes. Relative scale prevents rare outputs from
turning this correction into a rare rejection event. Third-order envelopes
pay for exact integer arithmetic, not only for input tosses.

The very strong conventional route is developed separately in
../broad_control/SHIFTED_REJECTION_PROOF.txt. Coarse positive proposals,
logarithmic coin factories, shifted exponential races, and capped relearning
already give the exact positive-factor endpoint, and extend to positive
arithmetic circuits and other models with an executable positive monomial
sampler. That route is ADOPTED, not claimed as a separation. The theorem below
does not require such a sampler or positive circuit representation. Its
arithmetic procedure may use subtraction. No priority claim is made for the
whole theorem; the literature comparison establishes the particular missing
operation investigated, not exhaustive novelty.

This is a theoretical construction with conservative polynomial constants.
The supplied programs verify the exact finite correction and a complete toy
factory; they are not a practical large-scale implementation of the generic
bound. A separate acquisition construction and actual numerical consumers
below prevent a hidden learned-representation or numerical-solver oracle.

check, and decisive acquisition/execution separation. Not proposed as the new
main Astra capability: qualitative model checking and support learning already
give much of this power. No priority claim.

1. Desired operation and strongest conventional route

From imperfect transition observations, acquire reusable knowledge supporting
later infinite-horizon reachability and physical reset/steering questions. The
strong conventional route is learned support plus qualitative/robust Markov
decision process model checking, not a finely estimated transition matrix.

Primary references:
* P. Ashok, J. Kretinsky, M. Weininger, PAC Statistical Model Checking for Markov
  Decision Processes and Stochastic Games, CAV 2019, arXiv:1905.04403v3.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.04403
  It treats unbounded reachability with a known lower bound on nonzero
  transitions, and also with known graph topology.
* S. Akshay, S. Bansal, G. Mahla, Certifying Almost-Sure Reachability in Unknown
  MDPs, arXiv:2610.18119v1, October 2026.
  https://arxiv.org/html/2610.18119v1
  Their certificate-transfer route computes hitting times of an estimated
  model and calibrates transition probabilities finely enough to transfer
  drift. Its worst-case sufficient calibration can be exponential in graph
  depth. The elementary support construction below avoids that calibration
  for producing some valid certificate, without estimating expected hitting
  times accurately. This does not refute a lower bound for estimating those
  hitting times or verifying an arbitrary candidate to a prescribed margin.
* PRISM official documentation, Uncertain Models:
  https://www.prismmodelchecker.org/manual/PropertySpecification/UncertainModels
  Robust interval-MDP verification already handles adversarial probability
  choices and policies; this is a strong executable conventional comparator.

# Paired drift can reveal an executable tensor factorization

Working construction and explicit prior-art qualification, 31 October 2026.

## Status and main result

This note constructs a reusable Clifford decoder from paired experimental
preparations whose individual-state average is maximally mixed. The paired
source changes from shot to shot, so it is not tomography of a fixed unknown
pure state. The construction is elementary, has a polynomial acquisition bound,
and is implemented in `twin_factorization.py`.

**This is not a claimed major new capability or a demonstrated advantage over
the strongest conventional method given the same paired observations.**
Aguilar, Jerbi, Eisert, and Bittel, arXiv:2609.27565v1 (September 2026), already
develop a polynomial Bell-quadratic-symmetry learner for Clifford-dressed
product pure states. Their quadratic lifting and algebra decomposition are the
strongest comparator. The source here is an ensemble of correlated twins,
rather than repeated copies of one pure state; its particularly simple
algebra admits an explicit kernel/image splitting implementation. This is a
useful constructive extension and experimental-interface observation, not a
substantiated claim of historical novelty. Ordinary adaptation of the published
method appears to deliver essentially the same operation on these observations.

The distinctive source property is that large shot-to-shot local drift can
coexist with exactly informative paired correlations. The quantitative result
uses the specified local two-design distribution; it does not cover every
possible drift law. The negative finding is
equally concrete: independent unheralded corruption of Bell outcomes destroys
the exact kernel. No general constant-noise robustification is established.

source draws independently Haar-random pure single-qubit states
